full_text_en:
Gao Senxiang Bribery Case

The defendant, Gao Senxiang, male, 50 years old, formerly the president of CITIC Industrial Bank Shenzhen Branch. He was arrested on August 10, 1990.

In the case of the defendant Gao Senxiang for bribery, the People's Procuratorate of Shenzhen, Guangdong Province, initiated a public prosecution with the Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court. After a public trial, the court found the following facts:

From June 1988 to July 1990, during his tenure as president of CITIC Industrial Bank Shenzhen Branch (hereinafter "CITIC Shenzhen Branch"), the defendant Gao Senxiang took advantage of his position to accept bribes in cash and in kind valued at a total of HK$1.723 million, RMB 630,300, and US$5,000 in the course of approving loans for enterprises or guaranteeing loans for enterprises. The specific facts of bribery are as follows:

In March 1989, Chen Minxian, vice chairman of the board of China Zhengxin Group Chemical Co., Ltd. and general manager of Fanxin Magnetic Plant, proposed to the defendant Gao Senxiang that CITIC Shenzhen Branch issue an irrevocable bank guarantee for a loan of US$3.2 million in Hong Kong, and offered a commission of HK$1 million. After Gao Senxiang agreed, he signed the bank guarantee on March 6. After obtaining the loan, Chen Minxian withdrew US$300,000 from it and remitted it to Chen Jianfan, manager of his joint venture shareholder Hong Kong Yongcheng Hang, and instructed Chen Jianfan to pay HK$1 million to Gao Senxiang in Hong Kong. Chen Minxian informed Gao Senxiang that he could collect the money from Chen Jianfan. In May of the same year, Gao Senxiang went to Hong Kong, and Chen Jianfan gave him HK$200,000. Gao Senxiang deposited the money in a bank using Chen Jianfan's Hong Kong identity card, personally signed "Chen Jianfan" on the deposit slip, and brought the deposit slip back to Shenzhen for his own safekeeping. Half a month later, Chen Jianfan took the deposit slip from Gao Senxiang and brought it to Hong Kong for safekeeping on Gao's behalf. From June 1989 to June 1990, the defendant Gao Senxiang subsequently collected from Chen Jianfan another HK$100,000 and US$5,000.

From December 1988 to January 1990, in the course of approving loans totaling RMB 27.9 million and US$7.6 million for Chen Minxian and guaranteeing other loans for him, the defendant Gao Senxiang accepted bribes from Chen Minxian totaling HK$120,000 and RMB 8,000.

From January 1989 to June 1990, at the request of Liang Sirong, manager of Guangdong Maoyuan Company and chairman of Shangxing Industrial Joint Stock Company, the defendant Gao Senxiang approved loans totaling RMB 31 million for Maoyuan Company and Shangxing Company from CITIC Shenzhen Branch. Gao Senxiang subsequently accepted bribes from Liang Sirong totaling HK$315,000, RMB 518,000, one Rolex watch, one Jiali brand color television, and one Dasheng brand audio system. The total value of the above cash and in-kind bribes amounted to RMB 522,300 and HK$335,000.

From October 1988 to June 1990, Chen Wenxuan, chairman of Hong Kong Yongning Company, introduced several companies that, with the approval of the defendant Gao Senxiang, obtained loans from CITIC Shenzhen Branch totaling RMB 19.7 million, HK$3.5 million, and US$4.9 million. Gao Senxiang accepted bribes from the borrowing companies and Chen Wenxuan totaling HK$798,000 and RMB 50,000. Gao Senxiang also asked Chen Wenxuan to arrange a Dominican passport for him, and Chen Wenxuan advanced HK$140,000 for this purpose.

From early 1989 to August of the same year, upon the introduction of Li Xinming, general manager of Hong Kong Chengxing Trading Company, and with the approval of the defendant Gao Senxiang, Meixian Zhonglv Storage and Transportation Company, Meixian Nongfang Company, and Baoan Wanfeng Development Company obtained loans from CITIC Shenzhen Branch totaling RMB 3 million and US$500,000. Gao Senxiang accepted a bribe of RMB 50,000 from Li Xinming.

From January to March 1990, Lin Longhui, manager of Shenzhen Fuxing Jewelry and Gold Shop, obtained loans of HK$33 million and RMB 7 million from CITIC Shenzhen Branch through the defendant Gao Senxiang. On July 24 of the same year, Gao Senxiang accepted a diamond ring from Lin Longhui in Hong Kong, valued at HK$30,000.

After the case was uncovered, most of the illicit money and goods accepted by the defendant Gao Senxiang were recovered.

The above facts are confirmed by physical evidence, documentary evidence, and witness testimony, and the defendant Gao Senxiang also confessed to them, which is sufficient for identification.

The Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court held that the defendant Gao Senxiang, as a state functionary, disregarded state law, took advantage of his position to accept property from others in the course of approving loans for enterprises and guaranteeing loans for enterprises, and his conduct constituted the crime of bribery as provided for in Article 185 of the Criminal Law of the PRC. The amount of bribery accepted by Gao Senxiang was particularly huge, and the circumstances of the crime were especially serious. Pursuant to Article 5 and Article 2(1) of the Supplementary Provisions of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on the Punishment of Crimes of Embezzlement and Bribery, he should be severely punished. In accordance with Article 53(1) of the Criminal Law, Gao Senxiang should be deprived of political rights for life. All property obtained illegally by Gao Senxiang, in accordance with Article 60 of the Criminal Law, should be recovered. Accordingly, on August 30, 1991, the court rendered the following judgment:

1. The defendant Gao Senxiang is convicted of the crime of bribery and sentenced to death, with deprivation of political rights for life.
2. All property obtained illegally by the defendant Gao Senxiang shall be recovered and turned over to the state treasury.

After the judgment of first instance was pronounced, the defendant Gao Senxiang appealed to the Guangdong High People's Court. The grounds for appeal were: (1) His previous confessions were fabricated subjectively and could not be used as evidence for conviction. (2) Among the bribes accepted from Chen Minxian of Hong Kong, HK$200,000 were collected from Chen Jianfan and deposited in a bank in Chen Jianfan's name. Later, the deposit slip was taken away by Chen Jianfan. It was improper to identify this sum as his bribery. (3) Among the bribes accepted from Liang Sirong, RMB 230,000 were directly given by Liang Sirong to Sun XX, which could not be identified as his bribery. (4) He had truthfully confessed his criminal acts, returned all illicit money and goods, and had reported and exposed the illegal and criminal acts of others; therefore, he should receive a lighter punishment.

After trial, the Guangdong High People's Court held that the specific circumstances of the bribery, including the time, place, and amount, as confessed by the appellant Gao Senxiang during the pre-trial investigation and in court, were consistent with the testimony of the bribe-givers and other evidence such as the recovered illicit money and goods. The HK$200,000 that Gao Senxiang took from Chen Jianfan was part of the HK$1 million bribe promised by Chen Minxian to Gao Senxiang for agreeing to guarantee the loan. Chen Jianfan, following Chen Minxian's instructions, gave the HK$200,000 to Gao Senxiang in Hong Kong, and Gao Senxiang voluntarily deposited the money in a Hong Kong bank in Chen Jianfan's name. Later, with Gao Senxiang's consent, Chen Jianfan took the deposit slip for safekeeping. After the case was solved, Gao Senxiang wrote a note instructing Chen Jianfan to return the illicit money to the procuratorial authorities. The above circumstances sufficiently proved that this sum was undoubtedly a bribe accepted by Gao Senxiang. In September 1989, Gao Senxiang's mistress, Sun XX, had a conflict with him and demanded RMB 600,000 from him. Gao Senxiang asked Liang Sirong to negotiate with Sun, and ultimately Liang Sirong gave Sun XX RMB 230,000. Afterwards, Liang Sirong told Gao Senxiang that this sum was a "commission" for thanking CITIC Shenzhen Branch for its assistance in obtaining loans. Therefore, the original judgment's identification of this sum as Gao Senxiang's bribery was correct. Gao Senxiang only gradually confessed to his criminal acts after the judicial authorities had already obtained a large amount of facts and evidence of his bribery. As for Gao Senxiang's reporting and exposure of "illegal and criminal" acts by others after his arrest, investigation revealed that some of the circumstances were so minor as not to constitute a crime, and some were found to be untrue upon investigation. In summary, Gao Senxiang's grounds for appeal were untenable, and his request for a lighter punishment was not accepted. The facts found by the original judgment were clear, the evidence was reliable and sufficient, the conviction was accurate, the sentence was appropriate, and the trial procedure was lawful. In accordance with Article 136(1)(i) of the Criminal Procedure Law of the PRC, the Guangdong High People's Court ruled on September 18, 1991: to reject Gao Senxiang's appeal and affirm the original judgment.

Pursuant to Article 145(2) of the Criminal Procedure Law, the Guangdong High People's Court submitted the case to the Supreme People's Court for approval.

In accordance with the death penalty review procedure stipulated in the Criminal Procedure Law, the Supreme People's Court reviewed the case and ruled on October 16, 1991: to approve the criminal ruling of the Guangdong High People's Court affirming the judgment of the Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court that the defendant Gao Senxiang was convicted of bribery, sentenced to death with immediate execution, and deprived of political rights for life.
